title: Proactive dispatch of rail maintenance equipment under weather-induced disruptions: an optimization framework integrating machine learning-driven risk assessment
abstract: Railway safety is increasingly threatened by disruptive events, especially those caused by extreme weather conditions. The growing frequency and intensity of infrastructure damage highlight the urgent demand for enhancing emergency repair responsiveness and optimizing infrastructure maintenance planning. This study introduces a comprehensive framework integrating railway risk assessment with maintenance equipment dispatch optimization, enabling proactive deployment of maintenance resources before weather-related disruptions occur. The proposed method employs machine learning to analyze multi-source data on track conditions, train operations, and high-resolution environmental information to forecast event risks across regional railway networks. This enables prior estimation of disruptions’ spatiotemporal characteristics, thereby supporting dispatch decisions through a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model. A case study using the Texas railway network demonstrates the practicality and effectiveness of the developed framework. Compared to reactive maintenance, the proactive dispatch strategy reduces the average repair time by 7.23 h, despite resulting in additional logistical costs. The benefits achieved by mitigating prolonged repair time significantly surpass the extra transport expenses. The proposed proactive strategy proves effective in accelerating the railway service restoration following weather-related disruptions. Furthermore, the concluding remarks provide actionable perspectives on both routine railway maintenance and emergency management, contributing to railway resilience enhancement and safety operations.

title: Stress-Diff: An advanced conditional diffusion model for stress field prediction in drilled flange connections under seismic loading
abstract: Drilled-flange connections (DFCs) are increasingly specified in steel frames because the weakened beam flanges suppress damage in the column or weld region and thus safeguard overall joint integrity. The severe stress concentrations around drilled holes create computational challenges: traditional finite element analysis requires extremely fine meshes and nonlinear solution procedures, taking over several hours per seismic analysis, which makes parametric studies and real-time design optimization computationally prohibitive. This study aims to develop a high-fidelity surrogate model that can rapidly predict stress fields in DFCs for future iterative design optimization. We present Stress-Diff, a novel conditional diffusion model that generates stress fields through an iterative denoising process. Stress-Diff includes four novel design philosophies: (i) a Fusion-UNet backbone that ingeniously integrates drilled holes’ layout, geometric and material vectors, and diffusion-step embeddings. (ii) a variance-regularized loss is additionally added that increases the prediction accuracy at the location with stress concentration. (iii) a self-attention mechanism in the latent bottleneck to improve the extraction of complex channel interactions. (iv) an optimized classifier-free guidance scheme that strengthens adherence to conditioning cues during inference to enhance the generation fidelity. After training on a self-developed FE dataset that spans realistic beam sizes, drilled-hole patterns and cyclic drift histories, Stress-Diff achieves a median MAE value of 0.033, outperforming the traditional deep learning method U-Net by 21% in MAE reduction and surpassing CGAN by 42% in MAE reduction on the test set. Stress-Diff generates a full-resolution (512 × 256) stress field 60× faster than traditional finite element analysis, with the average SSIM value of 0.92. Stress-Diff therefore provides a practical surrogate for rapid preliminary analyses, parametric optimization and digital-twin updates of DFCs, and the framework is readily extendable to other perforated or heterogeneous structural components. All the code and datasets will be released on GitHub upon publication.

title: Formula for irregular wave overtopping on vegetated seawall derived from physics-guided deep symbolic regression
abstract: Accurate prediction of wave overtopping for vegetated seawalls remains a critical challenge in coastal engineering, with no established empirical formulas currently available. This study bridges this gap by pioneering the application of deep physical symbolic regression (PhySO) to derive, for the first time, governing equations for irregular wave overtopping on these eco-friendly hybrid structures, providing a robust and interpretable tool for their design and safety assessment. Physical experiments simulating wave climates generated irregular wave overtopping data, establishing a foundational dataset for leveraging the deep physical symbolic regression algorithm to decode governing physical laws. The results show that PhySO was able to efficiently and accurately derive a spectrum of expressions relating overtopping to wave, seawall, and vegetation parameters, spanning mathematically parsimonious to physically interpretable forms. Through multi-criteria evaluation balancing simplicity, practicality, and accuracy, a robust predictive expression was established with R-Square of 0.74, Mean Absolute Error of 14.28, Root Mean Square Error of 14.52, representing complex vegetation-wave-structure interactions through dimensionless groupings. The applicable scope covering critical hydraulic regimes was systematically defined using experimental parameter extrema. Meanwhile, the physical significance of the derived formula is elucidated, revealing a reformulated freeboard dependence and a nonlinear vegetation attenuation mechanism.

title: Learning constrained static equilibrium for thrust network inverse form-finding via physics-informed geometric deep learning on CW complexes
abstract:
This work integrates Geometric Deep Learning (GDL) with physics-informed modelling to approximate solutions to a constrained, ill-conditioned, and nonlinear inverse shell form-finding problem across diverse geometries and patterns. Given a target geometry and pattern design as meshes, the proposed neural framework predicts a funicular shell—defined by edge forces and vertex positions—that satisfies static equilibrium and closely matches the target form.
Three main contributions are introduced: (1) a relaxed, numerically stable physics objective using efficient differentiable graph operators to mitigate the ill-conditioning of the nonlinear problem; (2) a stochastic augmentation strategy that enriches training with geometries of varying funicular feasibility, enhancing generalisation to infeasible inputs; and (3) a hierarchical GDL architecture that learns directly from irregular n-gon surface meshes, modelled as cell complexes to incorporate vertex, edge, and face features in both inputs and outputs.
This approach eliminates the need for simplification of graph datastructures common in existing methods, improving mesh modelling versatility. Extensive studies examine the numerical stability of physics formulations, robustness for out-of-distribution designs, and the expressivity of the GDL architecture. While focused on a specific inverse form-finding task, this work offers general insights into addressing ill-posed inverse problems, showing how physics-based learning can support optimisation of mesh-based architectural structures under variable connectivity and design constraints.

title: Automatic multi-anomaly detection of pipelines with ensemble deep learning-based computer vision
abstract: Pipelines are critical infrastructure playing critical roles in ensuring public safety and economic development. Pipeline inspection is an important way to early detection of anomalies for proactive and preventive measures to improve safety while minimizing maintenance expenses. However, traditional methods that employ pipeline inspection gauges and manual data analysis have inefficiency in cost and time. This paper presents an approach for automatic detection of four classes of pipeline anomalies via analyzing videos captured by optical cameras in pipeline inspection toolset. The approach uses a framework that integrates advanced generative adversarial networks, image pre-preprocessing, and ensemble deep learning techniques to address data scarcity challenges, achieving high accuracy and high efficiency. The effects of dataset size and data balance on the performance of ensemble learning models are evaluated. The approach has been validated using outdoor testing data unseen to the ensemble learning model, demonstrating high generalizability in detecting corrosion, crack, deposit, and intrusion.

title: Physics-informed band structure-integrated Continuous-time inhomogeneous Markov chains for stochastic occupancy modeling
abstract: Understanding and predicting occupancy patterns are crucial for enhancing the efficiency of building energy systems and supporting occupant-centric building design. Traditional discrete-time inhomogeneous Markov chain (DTIMC) models have been widely used for stochastic occupancy modeling; however, the assumption that state transition probabilities can change arbitrarily results in high model complexity and a potential of over-fitting. This study introduces a novel band structure-integrated continuous-time inhomogeneous Markov chain (CTIMC) modeling method based on the physical process of occupancy movement. The proposed method impose physical constrains on state transitions to confined neighboring states within infinitesimal time intervals, significantly reducing the quadratic model complexity to linear and improving interpretability and generalization ability. An extended band structure is further developed to account for the condition with rapid and drastic occupancy variation. The models are validated using a nine-month, high-resolution occupancy data exhibiting drastic occupancy variation pattern, which are divided into training and testing set. Results on the testing set show that the proposed band-structure-integrated CTIMC method outperforms the traditional DTIMC method in terms of daily log-likelihood. Notably, under high-complexity conditions, when the number of scaling coefficients exceeds 7, the DTIMC model exhibits severe overfitting, yielding log-likelihood values between –568 and –426. In contrast, the CTIMC model maintains robust under the same conditions, achieving substantially higher log-likelihoods in the range of –124 to –107. These findings highlight the potential of physical informed CTIMC models for robust stochastic occupancy modeling.

title: Towards transparent object detection models for construction sites: explainable AI and error classification
abstract: Construction site monitoring is essential for ensuring projects are executed as planned and achieving goals in productivity, safety, and quality. However, traditional manual monitoring methods are time-consuming, error-prone, and lack scalability. Deep learning-based object detection offers a promising alternative, but its “black-box” nature hinders understanding of detection failures. This study proposes a Grad-CAM-based explainable AI framework to diagnose and classify detection errors systematically. The framework consists of three main processes: (1) defining major types of detection errors, (2) collecting failed images for each error type, and (3) developing a machine learning-based classification model using Grad-CAM features and detection metrics. Unlike previous approaches that relied on qualitative interpretations, this study converts Grad-CAM heatmaps into quantitative features (e.g., GT influence ratio, activation-to-box distance, cluster counts), enabling automated error classification. Errors were categorized into abnormal viewpoint, small size, occlusion, complex background, and lighting variation, achieving 94% classification accuracy on synthetic data, 85% on real images, and 88% on AI-generated data. This framework enhances transparency and interpretability while supporting model optimization and adaptive deployment for real-world construction site applications.

title: Optimal energy management of buildings using neural network-based thermal prediction and economic model predictive control
abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems are significant contributors to energy consumption in buildings, directly affecting energy efficiency and occupant comfort. Traditional physics-based temperature modeling and centralized control frameworks often struggle to effectively balance the challenges of scaling across multiple buildings while minimizing operational costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel data-driven distributed control framework for the economical and resilient operation of the building community. Specifically, the framework employs artificial neural networks (ANNs) to capture multi-time-step nonlinear temperature dynamics, enhancing predictive accuracy for energy management across interconnected buildings. A distributed economic model predictive control (EMPC) strategy is developed, enabling local controllers to coordinate HVAC schedules in each building iteratively. This strategy minimizes energy shortages, optimizes overall community energy costs, and ensures thermal comfort. In addition, by facilitating energy interaction between HVAC systems, distributed energy resources (DERs), and storage units, the framework ensures electrical energy supply and demand balance during power outages. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy improves cost efficiency, resilience, and multi-step prediction accuracy, outperforming traditional physics-based EMPC approaches in coordination across multiple buildings.

title: AirfoilAgent: Airfoil aerodynamics optimization design via large language model multi-agent collaborations
abstract: With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) and next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in aerospace, ensuring their trustworthy application in aircraft design, operation, and safety assurance has become a central priority. However, deep integration of domain-specific design knowledge with intelligent agent algorithms, aimed at achieving more efficient and explainable optimization of complex aircraft configurations, remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, we propose AirfoilAgent, a knowledge-integrated intelligent agent framework for airfoil aerodynamic optimization. Recognizing the domain transfer adaptability of LLM-based agents within aerodynamic workflows, the framework decomposes the optimization process into three multitask modules: overall task planning, aerodynamic knowledge integration, and result evaluation and reflection. This structure enables an agent-oriented, end-to-end system encompassing airfoil parameterization, computational evaluation, and iterative optimization. For knowledge integration, the optimization algorithms are transformed into a multiscale interpretable aerodynamic knowledge system. Specifically, general systemic knowledge is extracted via retrieval-augmented generation, complex dependency networks among high-order geometric features are distilled as feature interaction knowledge using explainable machine learning, and dominant-effect knowledge is quantified through classical sensitivity analysis. Comparative experiments on lift-to-drag ratio optimization of a supercritical airfoil show that AirfoilAgent delivers an average improvement of 20.84%, representing a 10.59% gain over classical optimization methods. Beyond performance gains, this study demonstrates the feasibility of deeply coupling natural language processing, LLM reasoning, and engineering computation, thereby providing a new paradigm for trustworthy AI in aircraft design optimization with both high adaptability and strong interpretability.

title: TFD-Trans: Time-frequency hierarchical decomposition transformer for mechanical fault diagnosis
abstract: Rolling bearings are critical components in rotating machinery, and their health directly affects the safety and stability of industrial equipment. To improve fault identification under strong noise and complex operating conditions, this paper proposes a Time–Frequency Decomposition Transformer (TFD-Trans) for robust rolling bearing fault diagnosis. TFD-Trans integrates wavelet transform and Fourier transform within a signal-processing-informed deep architecture. A wavelet-driven frequency decomposition module hierarchically partitions vibration signals into multiple sub-bands, enabling fine-grained multi-scale feature extraction. A Fourier-driven autocorrelation encoding module then models global periodic dependencies in the frequency domain and enhances fault-sensitive representations. Extensive experiments on two real-world rolling bearing datasets show that TFD-Trans consistently achieves higher accuracy and stronger noise robustness than existing mainstream methods across multiple operating and signal-to-noise conditions.

title: TO-MambaLDM: Multi-physics informed Mamba-enhanced latent diffusion for cooling structure topology optimization
abstract: To enable high-precision 3D in vitro fabrication of medical hydrogel scaffolds, improving the stability and temperature-control performance of the cooling system in 3D printing equipment is essential. The channel layout of the liquid-cooling plate is therefore critical. Conventional topology optimization can produce feasible designs, but it typically depends on repeated finite element analyses, leading to high computational cost and slow convergence. Here, we propose TO-MambaLDM, a multiphysics-driven generative topology optimization framework that integrates a latent diffusion model with a state–space architecture. Compared with existing data-driven and diffusion- or Transformer-based generative design methods, TO-MambaLDM explicitly incorporates thermo–fluid operating conditions into the generative process and enhances long-range dependency modeling to improve physical consistency and connectivity. The framework captures thermo–fluid–structural coupling by conditioning the latent space with multi-channel field maps and boundary matrices. Mamba models long-range dependencies, while diffusion generates high-resolution, physically consistent designs. A manufacturability loss promotes channel connectivity and fabrication feasibility. Experiments show that TO-MambaLDM achieves a reconstruction accuracy of IoU = 0.93 and reduces temperature and pressure MSEs to 7.4 and 7.2, respectively, outperforming multiple baseline models, with improvements of 18.0% and 11.1% in temperature and pressure prediction accuracy. Transfer learning further verifies its ability to generate manufacturable, high-performance cooling structures across diverse inlet–outlet configurations. TO-MambaLDM establishes a unified, physically grounded paradigm for rapid cooling structure design in additive manufacturing, electronics cooling, and energy systems.

title: Large language models enable semantic-guided hierarchical games for intelligent battery coordination
abstract: The battery energy consumption system of lunar exploration rovers, as mission-critical equipment, confronts severe challenges under extreme environmental constraints. However, existing modeling methods face fundamental dilemmas: dynamic uncertainty leads to highly ambiguous constraint boundaries, making it difficult for traditional mathematical languages to describe complex coupling relationships; even when mathematical representations are constructed, high-dimensional nonlinear optimization problems become computationally intractable, with existing algorithms unable to address complexity barriers and lacking interpretability. In response to these challenges, this paper innovatively proposes a hierarchical Stackelberg game optimization framework based on semantic embedding. This framework transcends traditional optimization paradigms by deeply integrating the cognitive intelligence of large language models with the mathematical precision of game theory: large language models acknowledge that overall behavior cannot be predicted from simple combinations of parts, processing fuzzy constraints and cross-domain knowledge integration through semantic understanding; the hierarchical structure of Stackelberg games naturally adapts to the hierarchical decision-making requirements of battery allocation, with multi-agent game frameworks effectively handling coordination and competition relationships between batteries. Through semantic embedding technology, natural language constraints are automatically transformed into mathematical objects comprehensible to game participants, with cognitive intelligence handling the “incomputable” complexity components while game theory ensures “provable” mathematical convergence, synergistically achieving the important paradigm transition from “perfect rationality” to “bounded rationality,” thereby providing a theoretically rigorous and practically viable unified solution for intelligent decision-making in mission-critical systems.

title: Integrating segmentation and vision-language model for automated and interpretable building damage assessment from satellite imagery
abstract: The rapid assessment of constructed facilities after extreme events is a knowledge-intensive task critical for effective emergency management. However, methodologies for automated, object-level damage assessment at scale remain underdeveloped, often lacking fine-grained interpretability or scalability. This paper introduces a framework that integrates instance segmentation with temporal Vision Language Model (VLM), which is empowered with visual damage reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning on domain-specific knowledge, for the automated and interpretable assessment of structural assets from satellite imagery. Our three-stage approach synergizes: high-precision segmentation via a modified Segment Anything Model (SAM); spatiotemporal data pairing to isolate asset-specific changes; and BDAChat, the first temporal VLM fine-tuned for object-level damage assessment. Unlike traditional black-box models, BDAChat provides both high-accuracy damage classification and causal interpretations, serving as an intelligent damage inference system. The framework’s effectiveness and scalability are validated through the Lahaina wildfire and hurricane Ian case study. This modular framework automates and accelerates the object-level building damage assessment process, demonstrating significant potential for real-time building damage evaluation and resilient infrastructure planning. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/WangYong921/BDAChat.

title: Physics-informed embodied intelligence in the foundation model era: Advancing robot manipulation for smart manufacturing
abstract: In recent years, foundation models have emerged as a transformative force in artificial intelligence, enabling a paradigm shift in how robotic intelligence is conceived and implemented. However, despite rapid progress, the integration of physical reasoning into these large-scale models remains limited, leaving a gap between intricate manipulation tasks to complex manufacturing processes. Aligned with the current trends in robotic cognition development, we provide a comprehensive review of the theoretical foundations that underpin physics-informed approaches and analyze the architectural frameworks that merge data-driven learning with physical laws and constraints. By synthesizing the latest developments in both academic research and industrial applications, this paper highlights how the fusion of these domains not only enhances the robustness and interpretability of robotic systems but also accelerates their transition from simulation to real-world deployment. Furthermore, we discuss key case studies, benchmark techniques, and emerging directions, offering insights into the synergies and trade-offs inherent in current methodologies. Our analysis outlines promising avenues for future research, aiming to further bridge the gap between theoretical advancements and practical implementations in robotics. This survey positions physics-informed embodied intelligence as a critical enabler for smart manufacturing in the foundation model era.

title: A two-phase cost sensitive-based domain adversarial neural network for anomaly detection in mass customized production
abstract: In the context of globalization and intense market competition, detecting anomalies in products is vital for enterprises to improve quality, enhance efficiency, and reduce costs. Enterprises are also pursuing mass customization to meet personalized customer needs. However, customized products are typically produced in small batches. Furthermore, modern manufacturing processes typically exhibit low defective rates. Additionally, quality results are only available after the inspections. These characteristics lead to the challenges of small sample sizes, imbalanced data, and delayed label acquisition for production data, potentially undermining the effectiveness of existing anomaly detection models. To cope with these challenges, this study proposes a two-phase cost sensitive domain adversarial neural network framework that leverages transfer learning to apply knowledge from similar mass-standardized products to customized products. When process parameters are available but inspection results are not, an unsupervised domain adversarial neural network integrated with cost-sensitive learning is employed to address the issues of small sample sizes and unlabeled data. Within this network, the cost-sensitive learning component simultaneously tackles data imbalance by biasing the label predictor towards the minority class through higher loss assignment compared to the majority class. Once inspection results become available for some customized products, the label predictor loss for these labeled samples is incorporated to further enhance anomaly detection. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art anomaly detection methods in practical smartphone speaker and laptop solid-state drive manufacturing processes.

title: PE-MPINN: A parameters-enhanced multiphysics-informed neural network for data assimilation of seepage-consolidation coupling problems in spatially variable soils
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have been widely applied for solving inverse problems due to the powerful capability of integrating physical laws with data-driven learning. However, in the context of multi-field coupling processes in spatially variable soils, conventional PINNs still struggle to explicitly identify uncertain parameters and remain underexplored in engineering-scale applications. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a Parameters-Enhanced Multiphysics-Informed Neural Network (PE-MPINN) framework for data assimilation of seepage-consolidation problems in spatially variable soils. The framework integrates three-dimensional consolidation theory with random fields, using trainable Karhunen-Loève Expansion vectors to infer heterogeneous soil parameters. Furthermore, a parameters-enhanced subnetwork is introduced to iteratively refine these vectors to continuously improve the representation of soil variability. The proposed approach is validated on a core wall rockfill dam. Results show that PE-MPINN successfully assimilates monitoring and testing data, and accurately predicts pore water pressure, earth pressure, hydraulic conductivity, and compression modulus at engineering scales. Moreover, PE-MPINN demonstrates strong robustness under sparse, noisy data and varying heterogeneity conditions, while achieving superior spatiotemporal extrapolation accuracy. This study highlights the value of integrating physical knowledge with data assimilation by offering a novel, efficient framework for real-time seepage-consolidation analysis and geotechnical digital twin applications.

title: Physics-informed edge-enhanced temporal graph convolutional network for multi-risk evolution prediction in deep excavation
abstract: Accurate prediction of excavation-induced multi-risk evolution is essential for intelligent construction and on-site safety management. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Edge-Enhanced Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (PI-ETGCN) that seamlessly integrates mechanistic priors with data-driven learning for spatiotemporal multi-risk forecasting in deep excavations. During graph modeling, multi-source construction information is encoded as node attributes to construct a Multi-Source Risk Graph (MRG) that links heterogeneous variables across space and time. Mechanical laws governing wall–soil–pipeline interactions are parameterized with learnable edge coefficients, enabling adaptive modeling of spatial–physical couplings under varying construction conditions. During graph learning, PI-ETGCN combines edge-enhanced graph convolution with temporal modules to capture coupled data–mechanics relationships and spatiotemporal dependencies within the MRG. A physics-informed regularization term is incorporated into the training objective to promote mechanically consistent risk-evolution patterns and improve robustness and generalization. Validated on a real-world Shanghai Rail Transit project, PI-ETGCN delivers superior predictive performance, reducing errors by over 20% relative to the second-best baseline. Ablation studies further confirm that the proposed physics–data fusion strategy maintains high accuracy under limited samples, noise, and outliers. Overall, PI-ETGCN provides interpretable, decision-ready risk information for real-time monitoring and reliability-aware on-site safety management.

title: A dual-dynamic deep learning model with graph Kolmogorov–Arnold networks and Bi-GRU for seismic power spectral prediction
abstract: With the accumulation of earthquake records and advances in structural earthquake engineering, accurately predicting earthquake power spectra has become increasingly important for assessing structural reliability. However, conventional power spectral models struggle to characterize spectral modulation under varying magnitude–distance scenarios. As a result, they often yield overly smooth predictions that fail to reproduce spectral fluctuations and multi-peak structures, thereby compromising the accuracy of safety evaluations. To address this issue, this study proposes a dual-dynamic deep learning (DL) model that integrates dynamic Graph Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (GKAN) and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (Bi-GRU). The proposed model jointly captures similarity relationships among earthquake records and contextual dependencies along the frequency axis. Specifically, it adaptively constructs a dynamic K-Nearest-Neighbor (KNN) graph based on feature similarity to represent non-Euclidean associations among records under varying magnitudes and distances. In addition, leveraging dynamic graph learning and a dynamic fusion mechanism, the model performs bidirectional sequence modeling and adaptively reweights information contributions, enabling more effective capture of spectral fluctuations and multi-peak characteristics. Experimental results across multiple earthquake datasets demonstrate that the proposed model not only accounts for magnitude and distance effects but also accurately captures complex spectral variations, thereby improving predictive accuracy and generalization performance.

title: Robotic machining quality enhancement via physics-informed error prediction and collaborative compensation
abstract: Industrial robots have become indispensable machining equipment alongside machine tools due to their large workspace and high flexibility. However, their inherent structural compliance and geometric imperfections introduce spatially distributed pose errors, particularly in high-precision applications. Current robot error compensation is mostly based on single-source adjustment of the body, which is affected by the spatial sensitivity relationship between joint space and pose errors. For this reason, a hybrid manufacturing system integrating a robot and an external linear cell was constructed. Based on this system, a physical-informed approach for distributed prediction and collaborative compensation of robot machining quality is proposed. Firstly, a novel spatial–temporal attention-based sensing model was built to predict the robot pose errors. Secondly, an unsupervised distributed prediction module with physics informatization is constructed based on the sensitivity analysis of joint pose errors. Finally, the collaborative compensation is realized by a hybrid manufacturing system containing the robot itself and the external linear axes. Experimental validation on large-curvature surface machining demonstrates the system’s ability to simultaneously predict and compensate machining quality deviations, achieving positioning accuracy with maximum/average errors of 0.14 mm/0.03 mm respectively. The physics-based approach significantly outperforms conventional methods by coordinating distributed prediction with collaborative compensation, reducing sensitive joint adjustments while suppressing regenerative errors. These advancements establish a new paradigm for precision robotic machining in industrial applications.

title: DeSnow-GNN: Spatiotemporal graph neural network for robust LiDAR point cloud denoising in adverse weather
abstract: LiDAR sensors are widely used in autonomous driving and robotics but are susceptible to noise from adverse weather conditions such as snow, rain, and fog, which degrade their performance by introducing spurious measurements. Existing denoising methods, including rule-based outlier removal and 2D convolutional neural networks (CNNs), face challenges in real-time processing and handling sparse, irregular point cloud data. To address these limitations, we propose DeSnow-GNN, a novel graph neural network (GNN)-based framework for robust point cloud denoising in adverse weather. Our approach leverages a graph-structured representation to capture spatial and temporal features of point clouds, enabling efficient noise removal while preserving structural integrity. The model integrates a dynamic radius search for edge construction, a lightweight registration method for temporal feature extraction, and a motion gating module for spatiotemporal fusion. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets (WADS and CADC) demonstrate that DeSnow-GNN achieves state-of-the-art performance, with the highest precision (97.4%) and balanced F1-score (95.3%) on WADS dataset, while maintaining competitive recall (93.5%). Additionally, the framework exhibits strong generalization capabilities for other noise types, such as rain and fog, highlighting its versatility in real-world applications.

title: A physics-informed and stochastic KAN framework for car-following behavior modeling of human-driven vehicles in mixed traffic flow
abstract: The time-varying desired gaps of human drivers introduced intrinsic stochasticity into traffic flow, often triggering traffic oscillations and degrading the effectiveness of predetermined autonomous vehicle (AV) control strategies. To capture this characteristic, this study proposed a deep learning framework that embedded stochasticity into short-term trajectory prediction while reproducing realistic oscillatory patterns. The experimental mixed-traffic setup and corresponding AV control strategies were first established. The framework reformulated the loss function of a Convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (ConvKAN) and incorporated a stochastic sampler to generate trajectories from predicted probability distributions. A learnable positional embedding mechanism was further designed to capture spatiotemporal dependencies through the fusion of an initial embedding matrix and row-cross attention. To alleviate overfitting under limited data, a three-stage physics-knowledge embedding strategy was implemented, combining transfer learning with physics-informed neural networks (PINN) to preserve physical consistency while enabling data-driven learning. The proposed framework is evaluated through short-term trajectory prediction and traffic flow simulations. Results demonstrated that the constructed simulation environment, driven by the learned model and AV following rules, can reflect authentic flow evolution patterns. Additional analyses investigated the effects of AV penetration rates and intra-platoon positions on stability. Findings indicated that AVs effectively suppress oscillations, with stabilization improving as penetration increases. Although positional effects are generally limited, placing AVs at the head or tail of a platoon can further mitigate the amplification of speed variability.

title: Physics-informed LSTM-Transformer vision-enhanced system: Real-time axis prediction in tube free-bending manufacturing
abstract: The free-bending technique, distinguished by its exceptional flexibility in axis control, is emerging as a transformative paradigm for manufacturing complex tubular structures, overcoming geometric limitations inherent to conventional tube bending manufacturing processes. However, the high flexibility in multi-axis free-bending systems introduces nonlinear control complexities that critically compromise the tube forming accuracy. Real-time machine vision approaches enable in-process tracking of tubular geometric deviations, providing a fast method for axis prediction. To this end, this paper presents a real-time vision-enhanced prediction system that integrates with an LSTM-Transformer framework. A high-precision visual sensing system is developed to capture tube-end trajectory, integrating 3D-printed markers, depth camera, kinematic decoupling, and instance segmentation for accurate motion tracking and process parameter inversion. Subsequently, a physics-informed hybrid LSTM-Transformer architecture is proposed for dynamic bend axis springback prediction, incorporating trajectory-derived physical constraints and multi-objective optimization for spatio-temporal springback prediction during dynamic forming. Additionally, an online differential geometry mapping method for real-time curvature parameter estimation is introduced, eliminating the need for post-scanning and additional equipment, enabling closed-loop process parameter compensation during bending. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the mean absolute error of axial springback prediction by more than 60% compared to traditional theoretical models, with the mean absolute error for all groups remaining below 12 mm.

title: Data-driven inverse design of load-bearing 3D metamaterials via a physics-embedded machine learning framework
abstract: The inverse design of load-bearing structures that can deterministically change shape represents a complex, ill-posed problem in intelligent engineering design. This challenge stems from the non-linear mapping between target curvature and the metric tensor, which often leads to non-unique solutions. To address this, a hierarchical data-driven computational framework is proposed for programming the multi-scale geometry of honeycomb metamaterials. The proposed approach centers on a multi-fidelity physics-guided neural network (MF-PGNN). By explicitly embedding domain knowledge into data-driven algorithms, this method effectively resolves the one-to-many mapping from target curvature goals to specific geometric parameters. Using this physics-informed machine learning strategy, it is demonstrated that planar structures can be reconfigured into 3D surfaces with positive, zero, or negative Gaussian curvature through simple actuation. The robustness of the proposed computational strategy is validated through extensive simulations and experiments. The framework accurately constructs fundamental geometries—such as saddles, ellipsoids, and cylinders—with high fidelity (Normalized Mean Absolute Error, NMAE ≤ 0.016). Additionally, the MF-PGNN surrogate model achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) greater than 0.98 for forward predictions. Beyond geometric accuracy, the resulting structures demonstrate both large deformability and strong load-bearing capacity. This work establishes a scalable paradigm for the design automation and virtual prototyping of adaptive structures, with potential applications in aerospace, soft robotics, and flexible electronics.

title: Domain textual knowledge-enhanced few-shot utility tunnel video anomaly detection with multimodal large language models
abstract: Anomalous events in utility tunnels and other infrastructure systems are rare yet high-impact, and their detection is essential for preventing safety hazards and operational disruptions. However, the extreme imbalance between normal and abnormal events, together with the scarcity of labeled anomaly data, makes video anomaly detection both scientifically challenging and practically important for intelligent utility tunnel monitoring. Existing approaches either rely on large collections of annotated anomalies or learn only from normal data, often leading to limited generalization and poor interpretability. Meanwhile, abundant domain textual documents describing operational rules and risk patterns remain underutilized, as effectively converting such unstructured knowledge into actionable guidance for anomaly detection is still unresolved. To address these challenges, we propose a multimodal framework that integrates domain-specific textual knowledge with visual observations through structured reasoning. Specifically, we introduce a domain knowledge-guided question learning module that generates scenario-aware guiding questions from domain texts and aligns them with few-shot video examples via dual multimodal agent interaction. Additionally, we design an adaptive anomaly-aware sampling strategy to identify the most informative frames, thereby improving both detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, by grounding guiding questions in frame-level content, the system performs fine-grained, multi-step reasoning to deliver interpretable anomaly assessments. Extensive experiments on a large real-world utility tunnel dataset demonstrate that our method achieves substantial performance gains over existing approaches in this domain. Evaluations on additional public benchmarks verify the strong cross-domain generalization capability of the framework, highlighting its potential for broader deployment across diverse safety-critical monitoring scenarios.

title: An Open-Vocabulary Industrial Anomaly Detection method based on CLIP and LLM
abstract: Vision based Industrial anomaly detection (IAD) faces dual challenges of scarce annotated data and generalization of cross production lines in intelligent manufacturing. However, existing CLIP based open-vocabulary methods are limited by the semantic bias of manual templates and the blind spots in detecting multi-scale defects. In this paper, we propose a zero-shot IAD model with cross datasets generalization ability. It is an open-vocabulary framework based on Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) and Large Language Model (LLM). Firstly, a general anomaly-aware prompt learner has been developed to perform coarse-grained localization of general normal/anomaly patterns in images. Secondly, a LLM-driven expert prompt engineering has been constructed to describe the abnormal features of specific objects, where LLM is used to generate and refine standard prompt templates, and a multimodal fusion mechanism for object perception is utilized to solve the problem of insufficient semantic coverage of manual templates. Thirdly, a heterogeneous feature collaborative architecture has been elucidated to suppress the background noise. Finally, a test-time contextual scoring strategy is proposed to filter out low response abnormal prompt noise in the inference stage and improve the model’s ability to classify abnormal semantics. Experimental results on 6 public datasets have demonstrated superior performance of our model against other popular methods, where it provides a new technological paradigm for open-vocabulary IAD. The code will be released via https://github.com/1192207336/CLOVAS.

title: Mechanism-Driven vs. Data-Driven: A comparison of physics-informed bayesian estimation and deep learning models for EPB shield chamber pressure forecasting
abstract: Accurate chamber pressure prediction is essential for maintaining face stability in Earth Pressure Balance (EPB) shield tunneling. This study proposes a physics-informed Bayesian estimation framework that integrates a time-recursive physical model with two filters—the Bootstrap Particle Filter (BPF) and the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF)—to enable real-time chamber pressure forecasting. Using field data from the Shanghai Metro Line 13 West Extension, a comprehensive comparative evaluation is conducted, benchmarking the proposed physics-informed methods against a suite of advanced deep learning models. The comparison addresses multiple dimensions, including prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, data dependency, noise robustness, generalization, and interpretability. Results reveal a fundamental trade-off: deep learning approaches achieve high accuracy through offline training with large datasets, whereas the physics-informed EnKF and BPF demonstrate superior robustness, computational speed, and adaptability through online parameter updating particularly under conditions of limited data, noisy measurements, and unobserved geological variability. Interpretability analysis further highlights the strength of the physics-informed framework which provides mechanistic insights by dynamically predicting key parameters linked to excavation mechanics (e.g., muck apparent stiffness, discharge efficiency), thereby enabling real-time process diagnosis. Finally, this study suggest that the future of intelligent tunnelling lies in developing hybrid physics-informed control systems, which synergize the feature-extraction power of deep learning with the mechanistic stability of Bayesian estimation to enable robust, autonomous pressure regulation.

title: Multi-objective differential evolution algorithm based on partial reinforcement learning intelligence for engineering design problems and physics-informed neural networks
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative Multi-Objective Partial Reinforcement Learning Evolutionary Algorithm (MODEPRL). Unlike existing reinforcement learning-based DE variants that primarily focus on strategy selection or parameter adaptation, MODEPRL simulates intelligent behaviors observed in human or animal social groups through partial reinforcement learning (PRL). The core innovation lies in associating learners’ decision-making behaviors with adaptive score tables, enabling individuals to autonomously adjust their actions based on environmental stimuli defined by positive and negative reinforcement. This mechanism allows learners to collaboratively enhance the overall optimization performance. Numerical simulations on 27 mechanical design problems and physics-informed neural networks demonstrate that MODEPRL outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in global search capability, solution accuracy, and convergence speed.

title: Designing robust wind speed forecasting system under extreme Events: An Information-Guided decomposition and deep Learning-Based framework
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting under extreme events is crucial for minimizing the societal impacts of such events and enhancing the efficiency of wind energy production. However, most existing forecasting methods are primarily designed for non-extreme conditions, which poses significant challenges for ensuring the reliable operation of the wind power industry during extreme events. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid wind speed forecasting system under extreme conditions that integrates an optimized sequence decomposition method with a deep learning model, which is referred to as SKLD-RR-VMD-D-GRU. Specifically, the system optimizes the number of components in variational mode decomposition (VMD) based on the principles of maximizing the symmetric Kullback-Leibler divergence and minimizing the decomposition residual energy ratio, thereby yielding an improved decomposition method referred to as SKLD-RR-VMD. The optimized VMD is then used to decompose the extreme wind speed data, effectively filtering out noise from the original sequence. The decomposed sub-sequences are subsequently fed into a gated recurrent unit (GRU) network, whose structure is optimized using the dynamic time warping (DTW) algorithm-referred to as D-GRU. The final forecasts are obtained by aggregating the predictions of all sub-sequences. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated using datasets from multiple stations and compared against several baseline and advanced models. Additionally, the framework is tested with another alternative deep learning architecture, i.e., the long short-term memory, to assess its generalizability. The results demonstrate that the proposed system consistently achieves superior predictive accuracy and robustness across both extreme and non-extreme wind speed scenarios.

title: High-speed railway operational safety indicator assessment under earthquakes: a physics-informed hybrid prediction framework
abstract: In earthquake-prone areas, the operational safety of trains is under potential threat, making it crucial to conduct prediction and assessment of high-speed railway (HSR) operational safety for emergency avoidance. However, traditional numerical simulation-based assessment methods suffer from low computational efficiency and complex processes, while purely data-driven deep learning models lack physical mechanism support, resulting in poor interpretability and insufficient robustness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-informed operational safety assessment framework for predicting and evaluating HSR operational safety indicators under earthquakes. First, a train-track-bridge coupled dynamic model under earthquakes was established to generate sample data of vehicle safety indicators. SHAP interpretability analysis was conducted to obtain key physical information affecting HSR safety under earthquakes. Various modular static-dynamic feature fusion mechanisms were developed to improve the utilization of high-dimensional data features. Based on the derived physical laws, a family of weighted loss functions incorporating seismic wave characteristics and prior knowledge was proposed to enhance their focus on sensitive information. Finally, the improved framework was applied to multiple baseline models to verify its accuracy in sequence prediction and classification tasks. The results show that this physics-informed framework can accurately predict HSR safety indicators and classify over-limit conditions under earthquakes, providing a highly promising solution for assessing HSR operational safety in earthquake-prone areas.

title: Network-level pavement structural health monitoring enabled by a physics-informed hierarchical attention network and vehicle vibrations
abstract: The deteriorating state of extensive road networks demands cost-effective, scalable structural assessment methods to inform proactive maintenance. Moving beyond localized and expensive traditional surveys, this study proposes PhysHA-Net, a Physics-Informed Hierarchical Attention Network, for interpretable multi-scale health monitoring with potential application to crowdsourced vehicle vibration data. The current empirical validation is conducted using a single vehicle to demonstrate the methodology and the physical plausibility of the model. By embedding vehicle-pavement interaction (VPI) dynamics into a hierarchical attention mechanism, the framework bridges the gap between raw acceleration signals and structural performance. Comparative experiments against three baseline models, the proposed PhysHA-Net achieves a high coefficient of determination (R2 = 0.985) and a low Mean Absolute Error (MAE = 0.124). Notably, PhysHA-Net reduces the prediction error by more than 88% compared to standard data-driven attention mechanisms. The results confirm that the physics-informed layer effectively constrains the attention weights within mechanically plausible domains, providing a reliable and interpretable tool for network-level infrastructure management.

title: Real-time non-iterative component-level modeling of aero-engines using physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Real-time aero-engine models are essential for advanced control and health monitoring, which are extensively employed to enhance engine performance, safety, and reliability. A critical challenge in developing such models lies in the inherent trade-off between interpretability and computational efficiency: simplifying complex physics-based models or using data-driven models is often necessary for real-time performance, yet it compromises the interpretability typically offered by first-principles. To resolve this limitation, we present a non-iterative component-level physics-informed neural-network (NICL-PINN) architecture for real-time aero-engine modeling, delivering improved interpretability along with high computational efficiency. This method employs a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to approximate the component characteristics and matching relationships, rather than iterative solutions, while embedding a physics-based component-level computational model, incorporating the engine’s thermodynamic and governing equations, as physical constraints during training. By leveraging the MLP’s nonlinear approximation capability and computational efficiency without simplifying the underlying physics, this strategy simultaneously ensures real-time performance and interpretability. Comparative simulations demonstrate that the NICL-PINN-based models increase computational efficiency by 87.42 % compared to iterative physics-based models. Furthermore, under the condition of governing equation residual convergence, the proposed method reduces the mean absolute relative error (MARE) and root mean square error (RMSE) by at least one order of magnitude. Specifically, prediction of critical unmeasurable performance parameters, such as turbine inlet temperature, yields a MARE of 0.058 % and an RMSE of 5.31 e-3, while thrust prediction achieves a MARE of 0.135 % and an RMSE of 1.15 e-3. Furthermore, actual engine flight data verification results show that the MARE and RMSE for measurable parameter predictions are reliably below 1 % and 1 e-2, respectively.

title: High-dimensional design of kirigami patches metamaterials using physics-based machine learning with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Kirigami metamaterials show promise for diverse applications, but designing structures with targeted mechanical properties remains challenging due to the high-dimensional design space and the high cost of simulations and experiments. To address these challenges, we develop a method for efficient high-dimensional design using physics-based uncertainty-aware machine learning integrated in Bayesian Optimization. (1) Various kirigami cutting patterns are modeled using finite element simulations to obtain mechanical properties, forming an open-access dataset. (2) A physics-based spectrum-normalized neural Gaussian Process (Phy-SNGP), a hybrid machine learning-analytical model, is proposed for mechanical property prediction and uncertainty quantification. This model predicts coefficients that encode the physics-informed Poisson’s ratio–strain relationship under large deformation. (3) We improved the uncertainty quantification in Phy-SNGP by enhancing the data distance-awareness. The proposed framework incorporates uncertainty quantification and signed distance function–based space expansion for efficient design at target mechanical properties. The proposed design framework is used to design engineering structures: Two near-zero Poisson’s ratio kirigami structures maintaining constant width under large tensile deformation, and two wearable kirigami knee patches optimized for compliance and comfort during joint bending for human skin. All designs are validated through simulation and experiments.

title: Automated generation and surrogate modeling of 3D urban wind simulation based on physics-informed graph neural networks: a two-stage framework
abstract: The spatial configurations of buildings under strong wind conditions influence building energy efficiency and the surrounding microclimate. Full-scale and high-resolution simulations are severely constrained by substantial computational costs and time requirements. This study proposes a two-stage framework that integrates AI-based generative design with a physics-informed surrogate model for the rapid prediction of 3D urban wind fields. The framework automatically generates 3D community-scale building layouts using datasets from three Chinese cities. A dynamic-prioritization physics-informed graph neural network is then developed to predict wind pressure and velocity distributions. A T-shaped sampling strategy is introduced to preserve spatial fidelity while reducing computational costs. Evaluated on six 3D cases, the model achieves NRMSEs of 8.91% for pressure and 12.26% for velocity relative to CFD benchmarks, with a speedup of over two orders of magnitude. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of combining AI-generative design with physics-informed learning for efficient urban planning and microclimate evaluation.

title: An adaptive industrial large language model for mechanical fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions
abstract: Under variable operating conditions, mechanical vibration signals exhibit strong nonlinearity and time-varying characteristics. Traditional signal processing and deep learning methods struggle to extract stable fault features, posing challenges to early equipment fault detection and health management. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the Variable Operating Condition Large Language Model (VOC-LLM). The model builds a multidimensional vibration feature fusion module to embed time-domain statistical features, time–frequency domain entropy features and nonlinear dynamic features into the Transformer semantic space. It encodes variable-speed features to capture time-varying signal dependencies and designs lightweight adaptation for the large language model (LLM). This adaptation achieves efficient domain alignment with industrial scenarios while preserving pre-trained knowledge. The model deeply couples mechanical fault semantics with model inference logic to realize interpretable quantitative assessment of fault severity. Tested on both laboratory and industrial platforms, VOC-LLM significantly outperforms mainstream advanced methods. It accurately identifies equipment faults of varying severity levels, providing a practical and interpretable solution for predictive maintenance of industrial equipment.

title: Physics-Informed Multi-Fidelity Neural Network with Fourier features for three-dimensional flow field reconstruction in planar cascades
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional flow field reconstruction in planar cascades is crucial for the aerodynamic design of turbomachinery. Existing methods for obtaining flow field data, including experimental measurements and numerical simulations, have limitations such as long cycles and high computational resource consumption. Driven by the development of artificial intelligence, data-driven modeling has emerged as a new paradigm for cascade flow field prediction. However, single models rely on large amounts of high-fidelity (HF) data, significantly increasing the modeling costs. Although multi-fidelity learning can improve the prediction accuracy by fusing multi-fidelity data, purely data-driven knowledge transfer however exhibits insufficient accuracy in predicting complex flows and is prone to overfitting. To address these issues, this study proposes a Physics-Informed Multi-Fidelity Neural Network with Fourier features (fPIMFNN) that integrates physics constrained multi-fidelity learning. The framework implements a multi-fidelity collaboration network for cross-fidelity knowledge transfer, embeds the Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) equations as physical constraints to ensure prediction consistency, and conducts Fourier feature embedding to strengthen the capture of multi-scale flow features. Experimental results on a transonic cascade demonstrate that the proposed fPIMFNN outperforms various competitors, thus providing a data-efficient solution for complex three-dimensional flow field modeling.

title: Data-driven inverse design of aperiodic metastructures for tailored vibration isolation using evolutionary active learning
abstract: Traditional metamaterials often struggle to adaptively manage broadband random disturbances and specific frequency resonances for complex equipment under time-varying conditions due to their fixed bandgaps. To address this, we propose a physically embedded evolutionary active learning framework for the inverse customization and intelligent reconfiguration of non-periodic flexible metastructures using small-sample data. Specifically, a hierarchical decoupling strategy—training a Deep Neural Network (DNN) solely for local constitutive mappings and coupling it with physical transfer matrices—is proposed to fundamentally overcome the “curse of dimensionality” inherent in global designs. Furthermore, an active learning-driven closed-loop feedback mechanism is integrated with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) algorithm. Ablation studies confirm that, by dynamically updating the surrogate model through targeted physical validations, this closed-loop strategy achieves superior convergence efficiency and computational efficiency compared to traditional optimization approaches. Results indicate a coefficient of determination (R2) exceeding 0.98 on the validation set, with relative errors kept within 2.0%. The framework demonstrates a hierarchical “global customization-individual reconfiguration” capability. In the passive customization phase, the Pareto front autonomously provides a broad coverage of aperiodic designs to meet diverse isolation requirements. Subsequently, active reconfiguration was validated on two typical configurations selected from the Pareto front. For Configuration 1, current control significantly expanded the tunable ranges: attenuation constants to [0.39, 1.49], starting frequencies to [14.98, 41.90] Hz, and effective bandwidths to [21.74, 68.29] Hz. For Configuration 2, stiffness reconfiguration maintained high attenuation levels [0.51, 1.41] while enabling flexible adjustment of starting frequencies [14.03, 38.57] Hz and bandwidths [16.89, 47.98] Hz. Finally, wave mechanics and experiments confirm that this data-driven approach provides a comprehensive solution for intelligent vibration isolation in complex engineering.

title: Physics-informed event-frame fusion learning paradigm for high dynamic range 3D industrial metrology
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) optical metrology is essential for manufacturing quality and lifecycle management in intelligent industrial manufacturing. However, significant reflectance variations in industrial environments present a challenging problem for high dynamic range (HDR) optical 3D metrology. Traditional frame-based fringe projection profilometry achieves precise phase reconstruction on texture-rich surfaces but is limited by the inherently low dynamic range of frame-based cameras in ultra-HDR scenarios. Event-driven FPP offers robust HDR compatibility (≥120 dB), yet its event-based output, incompatible with conventional vision techniques, struggles to recover fine geometric details. To address this, we propose PhyHDR-DL, a physics-informed deep multimodal learning framework that integrates event streams and frame images for industrial 3D measurement. Unlike data-driven methods, PhyHDR-DL embeds two physics-informed priors into an end-to-end deep learning architecture (PhyHDR-Net): (1) an HDR simulation algorithm generating physically consistent training pairs under extreme illumination gradients, and (2) an enhanced sinusoidal-cosine component generation method extracting physics-aware features for event stream learning. Experiments show that PhyHDR-Net, trained on diffuse reflection scenes, enables ultra-high-resolution inference in unseen HDR industrial scenarios, delivering accurate and detailed phase reconstruction. Compared to data-driven approaches, PhyHDR-DL reduces phase reconstruction errors in complex HDR scenes, with mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) decreasing by 65.9 % and 11.05 %, respectively. This physics- informed fusion of frame and event data offers a novel solution to HDR 3D metrology challenges in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Physics-informed graph neural networks for sim-to-real structural response prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of structural dynamic responses under complex environmental conditions remains a fundamental challenge in engineering, primarily due to nonlinear coupling effects and the inherent limitations of both traditional numerical simulations and purely data-driven approaches. Conventional physics-informed neural networks embed physical constraints through loss function penalties, which may be violated during inference. To address this limitation, this paper presents a Physics-Informed Graph Convolutional Network (PIGCN) framework that implements hard physical constraints by directly encoding structural dynamics equations into the network architecture. Specifically, the mass and stiffness matrices are embedded into the graph adjacency structure to weight inter-node connections according to their mechanical significance, and physics-informed transfer functions derived from the structural dynamics governing equation are introduced to replace conventional activation functions, ensuring that every forward pass inherently satisfies fundamental physical principles. The effectiveness of the PIGCN framework is demonstrated through simulation-to-real cross-domain prediction experiments on two representative structural systems: flexible cables under platform excitation and spatial steel frames under multiple dynamic loadings. The model achieves R2 values up to 0.979 for acceleration predictions and consistently exceeds 0.924 for strain predictions, significantly outperforming conventional deep learning architectures. Notably, the model exhibits strong cross-domain generalization, accurately predicting real-world measurements using only simulation-trained data. This study establishes a unified and physically consistent deep learning paradigm for structural response prediction, offering substantial potential for intelligent health monitoring in marine and civil engineering applications.

title: A physics-informed digital design framework to enhance freeze–thaw durability of engineered concrete: A case study on basalt fiber concrete
abstract: The performance degradation of concrete under freeze–thaw cycles (FTC) is a critical durability challenge in cold-region engineering. Traditional empirical methods lack generalizability, while high-fidelity physical models are hampered by difficulties in parameter identification and high computational cost. However, purely data-driven approaches frequently yield unreliable extrapolations due to their black-box nature and lack of physical consistency. To address this, this study develops a parametric physics-embedded neural network (PPENN) framework integrated with a customized multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm, thereby forming an autonomous design system to enhance the freeze–thaw durability of basalt fiber concrete (BFC). The core innovation involves embedding a damage constitutive equation into the PPENN, enabling direct mapping from mix proportions to physical parameters. The trained model generates physically consistent predictions that are fed into the optimization algorithm to efficiently explore the Pareto frontier between economic cost and durability. Results show: (1) The model achieves higher accuracy on sparse/noisy data, with ablation studies confirming the importance of the physical decoding module; (2) The system successfully identifies complex cost–performance trade-offs and outputs corresponding mix designs, with the enhanced optimizer outperforming standard benchmarks in solution uniformity; and (3) Independent univariate freeze–thaw tests validate the system’s logic and feasibility. This work provides an efficient tool for frost-resistant BFC design and establishes a generalizable, performance-based framework for intelligent material prediction and development.

title: Physics-informed interaction attention enhanced residual network for reliable HVAC fault diagnosis under severe class imbalance
abstract: Reliable fault diagnosis under severely imbalanced data distributions remains a fundamental challenge in engineering systems. Conventional deep models often exhibit degraded minority-class recognition and unstable decision boundaries when training samples are highly skewed toward normal conditions. To address this issue, we propose a physics-informed interaction attention and efficient channel attention enhanced ResNet (PIA-ECA-ResNet), where PIA introduces a soft structural prior to model cross-sensor interactions among chiller operating variables through a learnable coupling matrix and sample-adaptive gating, and ECA provides lightweight channel recalibration to strengthen robust feature abstraction under data scarcity. To further improve diagnostic reliability for easily confused minority fault categories, a decoupled two-stage classification framework is developed to separate anomaly detection from fine-grained fault identification. Experiments on a benchmark chiller dataset with imbalance ratios up to 200:1 demonstrate that the proposed architecture consistently outperforms standard residual networks and conventional baselines. Under extreme imbalance, the model achieves 91.72 % accuracy and improves macro-F1 to 92.1 %, indicating enhanced class-balanced performance and reduced missed detections. With the two-stage strategy, overall accuracy increases to 93.6 %, while recall for refrigerant-related faults improves substantially, effectively mitigating false-negative risks. These results demonstrate that embedding physics-informed interaction modeling into attention-enhanced residual architectures provides a robust and generalizable solution for fault diagnosis under severe class imbalance, offering improved reliability for practical engineering decision support.

title: A collaborative deformation prediction method for multiple monitoring points of concrete gravity dams: physics-informed feature selection and multi-task deep learning model
abstract: Dam deformation serves as a critical response indicator reflecting the structural safety status of a dam body. Its spatiotemporal evolution characteristics are of great significance for the operational safety assessment and risk early warning of dams. However, existing deformation prediction methods mostly focus on single monitoring points and fail to effectively capture the spatiotemporal correlations among different monitoring points. Even multi-point modeling is often constrained by issues such as insufficient representation of physical knowledge, feature redundancy, and inadequate characterization of spatiotemporal collaborative relationships. To address these problems, this paper proposes a physics-informed feature selection and multi-task deep learning model. Firstly, a finite element model is constructed. Combined with Multi-Output Support Vector Regression and the Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer, joint inversion of material parameters for multiple monitoring points is performed to derive physically informed driving features. Secondly, a two-stage feature selection strategy is established. Robust preliminary feature screening via BorutaShap and SHapley Additive exPlanations-based incremental feature selection are adopted to refine key driving information and obtain the optimal feature subset for each monitoring point. Subsequently, a multi-task learning-based collaborative prediction model named Parallel Multi-branch Temporal Convolutional Network- Dynamic Cross-Channel Convolutional Block Attention Module-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (PMTCN–DCCBAM–BiLSTM) is constructed. The parallel multi-branch temporal convolutional network independently extracts the local temporal features of each monitoring point. The dynamic cross-channel convolutional block attention module is introduced to enhance the response of key driving factors, and the bidirectional long short-term memory network is used to capture the global spatiotemporal evolution patterns of dam deformation, thereby achieving accurate collaborative prediction of multi-point deformation. Finally, validation is performed using monitoring data from a concrete dam. The results show that the proposed model reduces the mean squared error (MSE) by an average of 94.37% and increases the coefficient of determination (R2) by an average of 9.47%. The proposed method enables multi-point collaborative prediction and constructs a unified knowledge representation framework integrating physical mechanisms, spatial relationships and temporal response laws. It provides a generalizable methodological foundation for identification of dam response patterns, anomaly attribution analysis and decision support for safety monitoring.

title: A physics-informed transformer with relaxation mechanism for robust tire force estimation across diverse road conditions
abstract: Accurate and robust tire force estimation across diverse road conditions is essential for vehicle motion control and safety. However, estimation performance is often degraded by transient dynamic mismatch, tire-road nonlinearity, and varying road conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Physics-Informed Transformer (PIT) framework integrated with a shallow Bayesian Neural Network (BNN). Unlike standard rigid physical constraints, a slack-relaxation mechanism is introduced into the dynamic residual to provide a structured relaxation for transient inconsistency between the estimated tire-force-induced dynamics and measured vehicle responses. The network is trained using a composite loss that explicitly enforces dynamic, kinematic, and wheel-speed constraints. Furthermore, the Bayesian output head performs Monte Carlo sampling to construct a prior distribution, which is then refined online through physics-residual-based updating to obtain a physics-fused posterior for enhanced robustness and physical consistency. Experimental diverse road conditions demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more accurate and robust tire force estimation than the benchmark methods under ice-snow, asphalt, and composite road conditions.

title: High-performance modeling of conventional and active hydrostatic/hybrid bearings: Applying coupled physics-informed neural networks (PINN) for reducing data volume and time costs
abstract: The study addresses the issue of improving the performance of fluid film bearing models, in particular hydrostatic and hybrid bearings, both conventional and adjustable. Data-driven models typically outperform numerical ones, but also require large amount of data and time for training. Applying physically-informed neural networks (PINN) for this purpose partly reduces the required amount of data and time costs when considering fairly simple bearing designs, mainly hydrodynamic ones. However, the problem is still acute for hydrostatic/hybrid bearings, especially having active design, due to a higher number of degrees of freedom. The study proposes an approach based on utilizing a combination of separate PINNs to reduce the costs of building surrogate dynamic nonlinear bearing models while maintaining the performance advantages. A relatively simple PINN-based model of a basic plain bearing is utilized at the first stage of the modeling process to calculate the hydrodynamic lubricant pressure distribution. At the subsequent stage, this distribution is modified by another PINN-based model taking into account the lubricant pressure in hydrostatic recesses. The proposed division of models reduces the dimensionality of the training dataset and shows an advantage over the numerical model in time required for solving a set of test rotor dynamic problems by approximately an order of magnitude with little difference in accuracy. The results are useful for design procedures for high-performance rotor supports, including active supports, reducing the time required for modeling, as well as for synthesizing such models.

title: A synergistic framework combining explainable AI and multiphysical simulation for uncovering process–structure relationships in mask electrolyte jet machining
abstract:
A significant challenge in advanced manufacturing is the deep, physically-grounded understanding of complex process–structure relationships, which is essential for robust process optimization and control. This study introduces a novel “Predict-Explain-Corroborate” framework designed to address this challenge within the context of Mask Electrolyte Jet Machining (MEJM). The novelty of this work lies not in the individual deployment of predictive modeling, Explainable AI (XAI), or physical simulation, but in their synergistic integration into a structured methodology to uncover and validate complex physical mechanisms. A systematic evaluation of machine learning models identified XGBR as the optimal predictor for micro-groove geometry (

The subsequent XAI analysis, leveraging multiple techniques for robust interpretation, provided transparent, physically-grounded insights into the process, identifying the dominant role of applied voltage and quantifying the significant impacts of edge effects and hydrodynamic influences. These data-driven insights were rigorously corroborated by multiphysical simulations. The practical impact of this framework is a clear pathway from black-box prediction to actionable, physics-based process optimization, with direct implications for improving manufacturing quality and consistency. This work establishes a structured, generalizable, best-practice template applicable to a wide range of complex manufacturing processes where the linkage between process parameters and outcomes is critical.
